# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 11 (Bi-Vb Ss11)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Ss11
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 11
**Title (English, from literature):** Accusing nuns of acting from bias
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-ss11
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Adhikaraṇakupita* constitutes the eleventh *Saṅghādisesa* disciplinary training rule for nuns (*bhikkhunī*) in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule concerns a nun who becomes resentful when a formal monastic legal issue (*adhikaraṇa*) is not settled according to her preference, and who persistently alleges that the community of nuns acted out of bias or partiality; upon formal admonition, failure to desist results in a Saṅghādisesa suspension [SuttaCentral]. In modern English, it has been translated by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this legal precept is shared widely across early Buddhist monastic traditions [SuttaCentral]. Parallels exist in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Ss 11) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Ss 11), as well as in the Bhikṣuṇī Vinaya and Pātimokkha traditions preserved in Chinese for the Dharmaguptaka (Ss 17), Mahīśāsaka (Ss 16), Sarvāstivāda (Ss 15), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Ss 14), and Mahāsāṅghika (Ss 15) schools [SuttaCentral]. It also survives in the Tibetan translation of the Mūlasarvāstivāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (Ss 14) and in Sanskrit in the Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* (Ss 15) [SuttaCentral].
In concordance with these textual relationships, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal matches between this text and the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi*, and shared legal formulaic material found throughout the *Samuccayakkhandhaka* (Kd 13), *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka* (Kd 20), and parallel Saṅghādisesa procedures in both the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Bu-Vb Ss 10–13) and *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Bi-Vb Ss 10, 12, 13) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus aligns passages cross-linguistically with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) and Vinaya commentarial texts, as well as Sanskrit versions of the *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and *Prātimokṣasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
